prompt: Use case: productivity-visual. Create a polished, slide-ready horizontal workflow infographic for the Metrology Workbench presentation. Extra-wide composition about 3:1, ideally 2400 by 800 pixels, with a genuinely transparent background outside the graphic. Three equal-size dark midnight-navy panels arranged left to right, linked by two prominent elegant right-pointing cyan arrows. Use restrained luminous cyan outlines, subtle depth, crisp white sans-serif type and immaculate alignment. Match a sophisticated scientific instrumentation presentation with navy, cyan, teal, and a small warm-gold accent at the final step. Within the first panel, a refined dimensional illustration of a precision bench meter and two compact current shunts with a clean waveform motif; within the second, an uncertainty-contribution bar chart with a small smooth distribution curve (conceptual, no numbers); within the third, a polished report page with neat table rows and a small gold check mark. These are compact recognizable illustrations, not detailed busy photographs. Each panel has its icon above a large exact label. Text verbatim, only these three labels: first 'Calibrate'; second 'Build Uncertainty Budget'; third 'Generate Report of Calibration'. Wrap second label over two balanced lines and third over two or three balanced lines, all labels same large typographic scale, very readable when placed across the middle of a 16:9 slide. All three cards and labels must be fully visible. Generous interior padding but minimal empty outer margins. Three steps occupy nearly the full image width. No title, subtitle, small descriptions, step numbers, logos, watermark, fake UI, extra words, or additional branches. Arrows clearly connect left panel to center panel and center panel to right panel. Preserve transparent alpha outside the panels and arrows; do not paint a checkerboard.
